test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 25 Nov, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A train travelling at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a pole in 24 sec. What is the length of the train?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Convert **speed** from km/h to m/s: 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.

When a train crosses a **pole**, the distance covered is equal to the **length of the train**.

Length = Speed × Time = 20 × 24 = 480 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 480 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the **train** = 72 km/h

Time taken to cross the **pole** = 24 sec

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0cde25f2d61d8eb9b9545b1e82611d81a48b449f928db0f7dec38b909fa24e1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed in m/s = 72 × (5/18)

⇒ Speed = 4 × 5 = 20 m/s

⇒ Length of the train = Speed × Time

⇒ Length = 20 × 24

⇒ Length = 480 m

**∴ The correct answer is 480 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing a Stationary Object with Length

When a train of length L₁ crosses a platform or bridge of length L₂, the **total distance** covered is (L₁ + L₂).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the **opposite direction**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. In the **same direction**, relative speed = S₁ − S₂.</p
